description: A director of student activities must approve the operating plan for a high-school spring musical and finalize the performance format, audience capacity, licensing, health safeguards, and transportation arrangements, with input from the drama teacher, facilities manager, school nurse, and family liaison.

shared_context.S1: The high school plans to stage its spring musical in the auditorium next month.
shared_context.S2: The draft production plan proposes a Friday 7:00 p.m. performance, 220 audience seats, ordinary stage effects, and optional event recording.
shared_context.S3: Ms. Morgan gives the binding approval for the production plan and its operating conditions.
shared_context.S4: The school's standard activity-approval process includes a planning check-in with the drama teacher, facilities manager, school nurse, and family liaison before the final plan is signed.

PF1.text: The rights holder for one musical number confirmed to Mr. Ellis by email this week that the school may perform it only after purchasing a live-performance license, and that any audio or video recording of the production is prohibited; Mr. Ellis has not yet attached the email to the activity-approval file.

PF2.text: The facilities inspection found that the auditorium may seat exactly 160 audience members for this production and that both marked side exits must remain clear; Ms. Rivera completed the inspection this week but has not updated the draft seating plan.

PF3.text: A cast member has a documented severe latex allergy, so all props and costume materials used in the production must be latex-free, and a staff member trained in the school's emergency-allergy protocol must be present at every performance; Nurse Okafor confirmed this in the student's health record this week but has not added it to the production file.

PF4.text: The district activity-bus coordinator confirmed that 12 participating students cannot reliably obtain evening transportation and that an activity bus is available for a Saturday 1:00 p.m. matinee; Mr. Shah confirmed this with the affected families and transportation office this week but has not entered it in the event calendar.

acceptance_conditions: The production must include a Saturday 1:00 p.m. matinee.
The live-performance license must be purchased before the production.
Both marked side exits must remain clear.
Props and costumes must be latex-free.
A trained emergency-allergy staff member must be present at every performance.
The final plan must contain formal records for licensing, facilities clearance, health safeguards, and transportation.

content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'licensing_record' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'health_safeguard_record' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'transportation_record' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The rights-holder confirmation changes the plan from ordinary performance with optional recording to a purchased live-performance license and a recording prohibition.
The facilities inspection changes the audience limit from the draft 220 seats to exactly 160 and requires a formal commitment that both side exits remain clear.
The health record changes the materials rule to latex-free and adds the concrete requirement that trained emergency-allergy staff be present at every performance.
The transportation confirmation changes the performance from the draft Friday evening event to a Saturday 1:00 p.m. matinee and requires a transportation record.
